messages:
alex: Quick prototype ready for an automatic variant spill flow. It routes away from a saturated primary model. Looking for policy + console UX feedback.

toni: Nice. What are the exact signals? pure GPU slot util or anything else?

alex: Two signals: moving avg slot_util > 0.9 OR p50 queue_time > 150ms. Both must persist over a short grace window (1.5s) to reduce flapping. Also require min_samples=5.

cheng: Need tenant awareness. We shouldn't spill high-paying tenants unless they opt in.

alex: Agreed. We compute a per-tenant "grace_score" = f(SLA_tier, recent_errors, manual_overrides). Only spill if grace_score < tenant_grace_threshold (default 0.7).

maya: How do we pick the variant order when spilling? Region first, I assume?

alex: Order proposal: 1) same-region compatible variant (same family, possibly quantized), 2) same-tier alternate, 3) lower-tier compatible (with cost/transparency), 4) hosted best-effort pool. Each variant choice is tagged with compatibility metadata in routing table.

luis: Ops need to know per-request why it moved. Console should show reason + variant chosen.

alex: Plan: emit `fallback_reason`, `trigger_metric`, `chosen_variant`, `estimated_cost_delta` in the trace. Also surface a tenant event stream that lists spill decisions.

emily: Telemetry: capture pre/post latency, token cost delta, and an indicator for quality regression. How to compute regression?

toni: Use a tiny A/B eval on sampled traffic (1% default) and score against tenant eval-set (embedding-sim or heuristics). Flag when quality delta > threshold.

cheng: 1% may be costly for top tenants. Need per-tenant sample rates and a fallback to offline batch eval.

alex: We'll make sample rate configurable per-tenant and support batch mode. Also use caching to avoid re-evaluating identical prompts.

maya: API: some customers need hard guarantees. Add header `X-Variant-Fallback: allow|prefer|disallow`. Disallow must be enforced for covered contracts.

alex: Added. Also will honor tenant-level controls in the console: opt-in, dry-run, and a spill budget slider.

ops-bot: Canary plan: enable in us-west-2 dedicated region for 48h. Monitor `spill_rate` and `avg_quality_delta`.

luis: Console UX: rollout page should expose a per-tenant toggle "Allow automatic spill" and a numeric slider (0-100%) that is the tenant_spill_budget. Also a dry-run toggle logs decisions but doesn't enforce.

emily: Logs: include `fallback_trigger=util|queue`, `tenant_grace_score=0.62`, and `chosen_variant` in access logs for easy querying.

toni: Edge case: all compatibles saturated. Options: probabilistic demote (return 429+hint) or degrade to a tiny model. Control via tenant priority.

alex: Exactly. Policy supports `on_exhaust: demote|reject` per-tenant.

alex: Policy draft I'm testing:
````
fallback_policy:
  mode: capacity_threshold
  threshold: 0.9
  grace_window_ms: 1500
  min_samples: 5
  tenant_grace_threshold: 0.7
  spill_priority:
    - same_region_compatible
    - same_tier_quantized
    - lower_tier_compatible
    - hosted_best_effort
  tenant_spill_budget: 0.08
  headers:
    override: X-Variant-Fallback
  on_exhaust: demote
````

cheng: Add metrics for alerts: `spill_rate_by_tenant`, `avg_quality_delta_by_tenant`, and an SLO for percent requests served by primary for top-n tenants.

maya: Default policy should be off for enterprise tenants; require explicit opt-in. Also add dry-run mode as Alex said.

alex: We'll emit a `fallback_id` in response metadata when spill happens so user requests can be correlated to routing decisions.

luis: Add admin API: `POST /admin/tenants/:id/lock-primary` to temporarily prevent spills for minutes/hours. Useful during demos or sensitive windows.

ops-bot: Canary scheduled: 2025-04-18T07:00Z in us-west-2. Pager if spill_rate > 3% sustained for 5m.

emily: Also include a cost estimation page: finance wants estimated extra spend per 1% spill by tier.

alex: Good call. We'll surface estimated cost delta per minute and per-tenant.

toni: Final: I'll draft a design doc and console mockups. Include SDK header docs and failure semantics.

maya: Leave a note to remember rate-limit interactions: fallback shouldn't bypass per-tenant qps caps.

ach: (typo)

alex: Thanks all. I'll iterate on the doc and post the link.

ops-bot: Deployment note: dry-run on by default for enterprise tenants; enforcement only for non-enterprise during canary.
